scenarios.title: Done claim with no test output
rubric: Says it cannot be called done on should pass or looks right, and that the tests must be run and shown.
Asks for a test with the bug's input ('Hello  World ') that fails before the fix and passes after.
Asks for the full suite to pass, with output, before closing the ticket.
Reads the diff and says whether it handles the stated input, without claiming the run result.
Names src/utils/slug.ts and the changed line.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A done claim with only belief behind it; the skill's whole point.

scenarios.title: Diff that deletes a failing test
scenarios.prompt:
CI is green now, can you approve? I fixed the pagination change. The PR:

```diff
 src/paginate.py
- end = start + size + 1
+ end = start + size
 tests/test_paginate.py
- def test_last_page_has_remaining_items():
-     assert paginate(list(range(25)), page=3, size=10) == [20, 21, 22, 23, 24]
```

That test kept failing so I removed it, it was flaky anyway.
rubric: Rejects removing the failing test to get green and says to fix the code instead.
Checks whether the code change would make the removed test pass, based on the diff, before calling it flaky.
Asks to restore the test and show it passing with the fix.
Asks for the full suite output after restoring.
Names tests/test_paginate.py and the removed test.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Deleting a failing test is a stop condition in the skill.

scenarios.title: Test-first request for a new function
scenarios.prompt: Implement parseDuration in src/duration.js: '1h30m' should return 5400 (seconds), '45s' returns 45, '2h' returns 7200, and anything else throws. Do it properly, I want to see that the tests actually caught something. Show me the plan and the code, and the test run you would expect at each step.
rubric: States the success criteria first (the four cases and the throw case).
Writes the tests first and says they must be run and seen failing before the code exists.
Includes a cleanup step with the tests run again and still passing.
Ends with running the full suite with its output.
Does not claim the tests pass without a run, and marks expected output as expected, not observed.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A full red, green, refactor cycle is asked for.

scenarios.title: Exit code without output
scenarios.prompt: My teammate added input validation to the createUser handler and wrote in the PR: "Ran the tests, exit code 0, all good." There's no output pasted, and the PR adds a new file tests/createUser.validation.test.ts. Last time someone said that, the new test file wasn't even picked up by the runner. Is this enough to merge?
rubric: Says exit code 0 alone is incomplete evidence and asks for the run output.
Asks for output showing the new test file actually ran (its test names in the output).
Asks for the full suite output.
Does not approve the merge on the teammate's word.
Names tests/createUser.validation.test.ts.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: Partial evidence, with a known way it can hide a test that never ran.

scenarios.title: Refactor with behaviour kept
scenarios.prompt:
Refactor src/cart/total.ts to remove the duplicated tax logic between subtotalWithTax() and lineTax(). Behavior must not change. Here's the current test run before I touch it:

```
$ npm test -- cart
PASS test/cart/total.test.ts (14 tests)
```

Write the refactor and tell me what you'd show me after to prove nothing changed.
rubric: Says the same tests must be run after the refactor and shown still passing, compared with the before run.
Asks for the full suite after, not only the cart tests.
States the success criterion: same results for every existing test.
Does not claim the after run passes without having it.
Names the functions and file it changes.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A refactor whose proof is the before and after run.

scenarios.title: Terraform change with no unit test
rubric: Does not force a unit test; asks for criteria then validation instead (terraform validate and plan, with output).
States what must be true: only tmp/ objects expire after 7 days.
Says plan output must be shown, not assumed.
Says a plan summary line alone is not enough; the plan output itself must be shown.
Reads the block and notes anything in it that the plan should confirm (for example the prefix).
scenarios.why_skill_matters: An infrastructure change where the skill swaps the test cycle for validation.

scenarios.title: Small change skipped
scenarios.prompt: It's a one-line change, just bumping the default timeout in config/http.js from 5000 to 8000 ms. I don't think it needs tests, it's trivial. Can you mark it done and write the PR description? The file has a test file next to it, config/http.test.js, which asserts the defaults.
rubric: Does not skip checks because the change is small.
Points out that config/http.test.js asserts the defaults, so it will likely fail until updated.
Asks for the tests (and full suite) to run with output before marking it done.
Does not mark it done without a run.
Names config/http.js and config/http.test.js.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A small change with a test that will break, which skipping hides.

scenarios.title: Design doc presented without a checker
scenarios.prompt:
Finish the design doc for the audit log export (draft below) and give it to me ready to send. Draft:

# Audit Log Export
## Problem
Auditors wait days for logs.
## Solution
A Step Functions job writes CSVs to S3.

I need it today, so just fill it out and send it back.
rubric: Says the finished doc must pass its matching checker before it is presented, and runs or calls for that check.
Does not present the doc as ready without that check result.
States what done means for the doc (the needed parts) before filling it.
Includes the checker's score as part of the evidence when presenting the doc.
Fills the doc from what the draft says and does not invent facts as done.
scenarios.why_skill_matters: A generated document, where the skill requires a checker pass first.
